_note: v2 hook overrides for la Montée des Habitudes (ST_habitudes, S02_home), a stepped autumn alley climbing the hillside (ST_routine seg010-014). Every hook describes what is actually painted (nothing is written in the paintings): Monsieur Verbe the striped mime acts out each verb; there are no reflexives on this street, so no hand mirror.

fr_adopter_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe lifts a puppy out of the basket and hugs it: he ADOPTS it, a new member of the family (ah-dop-TAY).
fr_adopter_verb.why: ADOPT → adopter = to adopt (ils ont adopté un chien); also to pass, to vote through (adopter une loi). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_supprimer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe drops the rotten apple into the crate with a grimace: gone, DELETED, SUPPRESSED (sew-pree-MAY).
fr_supprimer_verb.why: SUPPRESS → supprimer = to delete, to remove, to abolish (j'ai supprimé ce message). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_decrocher_verb.hook: Ring ring! Monsieur Verbe UNHOOKS the receiver from the old wall telephone: he picks up, off the CROCHET hook (day-kroh-SHAY).
fr_decrocher_verb.why: Un crochet (a hook) → décrocher = to unhook, to take down; to pick up the phone (il décroche le téléphone). Opposite: raccrocher = to hang up. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_succomber_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe closes his eyes and lifts a forkful of the chocolate cake: he SUCCUMBS to temptation (sew-kohn-BAY).
fr_succomber_verb.why: SUCCUMB → succomber = to succumb, to give in (j'ai succombé à la tentation); also to die of (succomber à ses blessures). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_fondre_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe stares in dismay as his pink ice cream MELTS and drips down the cone: FONDUE-runny (FOHNDR).
fr_fondre_verb.why: FOUND (a foundry melts metal), fondue → fondre = to melt (la neige fond au soleil); fondre en larmes = to burst into tears. PURPLE beret = regular -re (je fonds, nous fondons).

fr_user_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe holds up his old trainer, full of holes: he has USED it until it is WORN OUT (ew-ZAY).
fr_user_verb.why: USE (up) → user = to wear out (il a usé ses chaussures); usé = worn, threadbare; l'usure = wear and tear. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_gaspiller_verb.hook: Whistling with his back turned, Monsieur Verbe lets the pump GUSH and SPILL over the bucket: what a WASTE (gahs-pih-YAY).
fr_gaspiller_verb.why: GASP + SPILL → gaspiller = to waste (il ne faut pas gaspiller l'eau); le gaspillage = waste. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_flatter_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe pats and strokes the happy dog, who FLATTENS its ears with joy: he CARESSES it, and FLATTERS it too (flah-TAY).
fr_flatter_verb.why: FLATTER → flatter = to flatter; to stroke, to pat an animal (il flatte son chien). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_tricher_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe slips a checker across the board with a sly grin while the cat looks away: a TRICKY CHEAT (tree-SHAY).
fr_tricher_verb.why: TRICK → tricher = to cheat (il ne faut pas tricher au jeu); un tricheur = a cheat. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_chausser_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe pulls on a green welly: he PUTS ON his footwear, like CHAUSSURES (shoes) (shoh-SAY).
fr_chausser_verb.why: Une chaussure (a shoe) → chausser = to put on shoes or boots (il chausse ses bottes); je chausse du 42 = I take a size 42. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_deplier_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe UNFOLDS the big map: un-PLY it, flat open (day-plee-YAY).
fr_deplier_verb.why: Dé + plier (to fold, PLY) → déplier = to unfold (il déplie la carte). Opposite: plier. RED beret = regular -er. (nous déplions).

fr_epuiser_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe slumps on the step, tongue out and sweating: the climb has EXHAUSTED him, his well run dry, like a PUITS (well) pumped empty (ay-pwee-ZAY).
fr_epuiser_verb.why: Un puits (a well) → épuiser = to exhaust, to wear out; to use up (les stocks sont épuisés = sold out). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_deployer_verb.hook: Beside the heron spreading its great wings, Monsieur Verbe SPREADS his arms wide too: they DEPLOY together (dayp-lwah-YAY).
fr_deployer_verb.why: DEPLOY → déployer = to spread out, to unfold, to deploy (l'oiseau déploie ses ailes). RED beret = regular -er. (je déploie, nous déployons). Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (day-plwah-YAY -> dayp-lwah-YAY).

fr_faillir_verb.hook: Oops! Monsieur Verbe catches his foot on a stone and ALMOST falls: he very nearly FAILS to keep his feet (fah-YEER).
fr_faillir_verb.why: FAIL → faillir + infinitive = to almost do (j'ai failli tomber = I nearly fell). GOLD beret = irregular (j'ai failli; mostly used in the passé composé).

fr_motiver_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe waves his red pom-poms and cheers the tortoise on: he MOTIVATES it up the steps (moh-tee-VAY).
fr_motiver_verb.why: MOTIVATE → motiver = to motivate (le coach motive son équipe); also to justify, to give grounds for. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_suspendre_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe reached up to hang the lantern on the branch and is left dangling from it himself, SUSPENDED in mid-air (sews-PAHNDR).
fr_suspendre_verb.why: SUSPEND → suspendre = to hang up (elle suspend le linge); also to suspend, to break off (la séance est suspendue). PURPLE beret = regular -re (je suspends, nous suspendons).

fr_heberger_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe carries the old lady's suitcase toward the guest room with its cozy bed: he is putting her up, like a HARBORING HOST at an inn (ay-behr-ZHAY).
fr_heberger_verb.why: Héberger = to house, to put someone up (mes amis m'hébergent); l'hébergement = accommodation; also to host a website. RED beret = regular -er. (nous hébergeons).

fr_arracher_verb.hook: Heave! Monsieur Verbe PULLS UP a giant carrot, soil flying: he RIPS it out by the roots (ah-rah-SHAY).
fr_arracher_verb.why: Arracher = to pull out, to tear out, to uproot (le dentiste m'a arraché une dent). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_incendier_verb.hook: The goat is chewing the poster, and Monsieur Verbe, red as a flame, gives it a fiery telling-off: he ROASTS it, as in an INCENDIARY rage (an-sahn-DYAY).
fr_incendier_verb.why: INCENDIARY → incendier = to set fire to, to burn down (the main meaning); also, informally, to give someone a roasting (il s'est fait incendier). Un incendie = a fire. RED beret = regular -er. (nous incendions).

fr_barrer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe sets a striped BARRIER across the steps: they are BARRED (bah-RAY).
fr_barrer_verb.why: BAR → barrer = to bar, to block (une voiture barre la route); also to cross out (barrer un mot). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_chauffer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe sets the copper kettle on the closed iron stove to HEAT, like a CHAUFFEUR stoking an engine (shoh-FAY).
fr_chauffer_verb.why: Chaud (hot) → chauffer = to heat, to warm (je fais chauffer de l'eau); le chauffage = heating; le chauffeur once stoked the boiler. RED beret = regular -er.

fr_redescendre_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe goes back DOWN the steps with his basket: he RE-DESCENDS (ruh-day-SAHNDR).
fr_redescendre_verb.why: Re + DESCEND → redescendre = to come back down, to go down again (nous redescendons de la montagne). PURPLE beret = regular -re (je redescends, nous redescendons).

fr_afficher_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe pins a cat poster up on the notice board: he puts it up, AFFIXES it on display (ah-fee-SHAY).
fr_afficher_verb.why: AFFIX, une affiche (a poster) → afficher = to put up, to display (les résultats sont affichés à l'entrée). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_accourir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe RUSHES UP to the puppy, arms out: A-COURSE-ing toward it at a run (ah-koo-REER).
fr_accourir_verb.why: À + courir (to run, COURSE) → accourir = to rush up, to come running (les enfants accourent vers leur père). GOLD beret = irregular (like courir: j'accours, nous accourons; il est accouru).

fr_amenager_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe carries a little bed into the empty summerhouse: he is FITTING it OUT as a bedroom, to be MANAGED as a new room (ah-may-nah-ZHAY).
fr_amenager_verb.why: À + ménage (household) → aménager = to fit out, to convert, to lay out (ils aménagent le grenier en chambre). RED beret = regular -er. (nous aménageons).

fr_emballer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe in a pink tutu does BALLET on tiptoe while he WRAPS a present: ahn-bah-LAY = (en) ballet.
fr_emballer_verb.why: En + balle (a BALE) → emballer = to wrap up, to pack (j'emballe le cadeau); informally, to thrill (ça m'emballe !). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_veiller_verb.hook: Late at night, by the glowing lantern in the summerhouse, Monsieur Verbe stays up WATCHING OVER the garden while the kitten sleeps: a VIGIL (vay-YAY).
fr_veiller_verb.why: VIGIL → veiller = to stay up; to watch over (elle veille sur ses enfants); la veille = the day before (the eve). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_contaminer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe tips green ink into the clear pitcher of water: now the water is CONTAMINATED (kohn-tah-mee-NAY).
fr_contaminer_verb.why: CONTAMINATE → contaminer = to contaminate, to infect (l'eau de la rivière est contaminée). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_rincer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe RINSES the carrots under the pump (ran-SAY).
fr_rincer_verb.why: RINSE → rincer = to rinse (rince bien les légumes). RED beret = regular -er. (nous rinçons).
